papers.title: Structural anti-Asian racism, structural cisheterosexism, and psychological, behavioral, and sleep health among Asian American sexual and gender minority adolescents.
papers.abstract: Since the COVID-19 pandemic began, a dramatic rise in anti-Asian sentiment as well as cissemxism and heterosexism (hereafter, cisheterosexism) has been documented, particularly affecting Asian American (AA) sexual and gender minority (SGM) adolescents who face intersecting oppressions. We investigated the associations between state-level structural anti-Asian racism, structural cisheterosexism, and psychological, behavioral, and sleep health outcomes among AA SGM adolescents. This study analyzed a subsample of AA SGM adolescents (N = 980) from a US cross-sectional national survey of 17 578 SGM adolescents aged 13-18 years old conducted in 2022. To quantify state-level structural anti-Asian racism and structural cisheterosexism, we utilized data from multiple sources including Project Implicit (implicit and explicit prejudiced attitudes), Education Week (critical race theory legislation), and Movement Advancement Project (anti-SGM laws and policies). Multivariate regression analyses examined associations between structural oppression and health outcomes, adjusting for individual demographics and state-level covariates (poverty, income inequality, conservatism, and population density). Higher levels of structural anti-Asian racism were associated with greater psychological distress (adjusted b = 0.58, robust SE = 0.21) and higher odds of recent vape use (adjusted odds ratio = 2.56, 95% CI: 1.77-3.70). Structural cisheterosexism was associated with greater odds of past-year alcohol use (adjusted OR = 2.07, 95% CI: 1.27-3.38), but less sleep trouble (adjusted b = -0.31, robust SE = 0.08). The adverse effects of structural anti-Asian racism on psychological distress were amplified for AA SGM adolescents living in states with higher structural cisheterosexism. These findings demonstrate how intersecting structural oppressions shape health outcomes among multiply marginalized youth, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive policies addressing multiple forms of structural oppressions.

papers.title: A randomized pilot trial of non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation: EEG activity and cognitive outcomes in cognitively normal older adults.
papers.abstract: BackgroundGamma-frequency (40 Hz) sensory stimulation is a promising non-pharmacological approach for modulating neural activity and cognitive function in aging and Alzheimer's disease. However, conventional flickering stimulation is often poorly tolerated, and evidence for non-flickering approaches remains limited.ObjectiveTo evaluate the neurophysiological and cognitive effects of 4-week (28-session) non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation in cognitively normal older adults.MethodsIn this randomized, double-blind, active-controlled pilot trial, 33 cognitively normal older adults were assigned to receive either non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation (n = 17) or a 70 Hz active-controlled condition (n = 16) over four weeks. Per-protocol analyses were conducted in 29 participants who completed the intervention. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) was acquired at baseline, immediately after the first intervention session, and after completion of the 4-week intervention. Neuropsychological assessments were performed at baseline and after the intervention. Prespecified primary outcomes were resting-state gamma-band power spectral density (PSD) and functional connectivity (FC).ResultsNo significant between-group differences were observed in resting-state gamma-band PSD or FC following either one-session or 28-session intervention. Unadjusted secondary analyses suggested potential improvements in selected episodic memory measures in the 40 Hz group. Exploratory analyses further identified a positive association between improvements in visuospatial memory and increases in occipital-temporal FC. Both interventions were well tolerated.ConclusionsA 28-session non-flickering 40 Hz light stimulation was well tolerated and may improve selected episodic memory measures in cognitively normal older adults. Although no measurable group-level EEG effects were observed, the exploratory cognitive findings warrant further investigation in larger randomized trials.ClinicalTrial.gov (ID: NCT06715995) https://clinicaltrials.gov/expert-search?term=NCT06715995.

papers.title: Melatonin as a potential biomarker for subclinical epileptiform activity in Alzheimer's disease: An exploratory study.
papers.abstract: BackgroundMelatonin levels are altered in elderly people and might become even more disrupted in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients. An inverse correlation between cerebrospinal fluid melatonin levels and severity of AD neuropathology has been described. There is an increased prevalence of subclinical epileptiform activity (SEA) in AD. Baseline melatonin levels have been described to be lower in epilepsy patients as compared to controls, suggesting antiepileptic effects.ObjectiveTo compare melatonin levels between AD participants and controls, to evaluate melatonin's potential use as biomarker for disease stage in AD and to evaluate the link between melatonin levels and SEA in AD.MethodsAD subjects (n = 20) and healthy volunteers (n = 8) underwent a 24-h-electro-encephalography (EEG), during which multiple blood and saliva samples were taken. Melatonin levels were analysed using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (plasma) and radioimmunoassay (saliva). A subset of participants underwent 50-min resting magnetoencephalography and/or high-density-EEG to detect SEA.ResultsPlasma melatonin levels were significantly lower in AD as compared to controls at 23:00PM. Melatonin levels were similar between patients with AD dementia, MCI due to AD and preclinical AD subjects. Plasma and saliva melatonin levels at 04:00AM and 01:00AM, respectively, were significantly higher in AD participants with SEA as compared to those without.ConclusionsNight-time melatonin levels might serve as a potential biomarker to identify AD patients at risk for SEA, based on exploratory findings. Whether this increase could be a compensatory feedback mechanism against SEA or whether melatonin rather has pro-epileptic effects, remains to be elucidated by further research.

papers.title: The Sleepless Watch: Perceived Sleep Quality of Nurses Working in High-Intensity Settings.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality is a global health concern among nurses, particularly in high-intensity settings. Unpredictable workloads, extended shifts and high patient acuity compromise sleep quality, negatively affecting nurses' well-being and patient outcomes. To describe the perceived sleep quality of nurses working in high-intensity settings. A qualitative descriptive design was used. Purposive sampling was used to select participants who met the inclusion criteria. Data were collected through three semi-structured focus group discussions with 21 nurses working in high-intensity units of an academic hospital in Gauteng, South Africa. Thematic analysis was used to analyse data manually, and the COREQ guidelines were followed. Three major themes emerged: barriers to quality sleep, consequences of poor sleep and coping mechanisms. Participants described environmental, occupational, organisational and domestic barriers to quality sleep, including community noise, long working hours, staff shortages, inadequate resources and family responsibilities. Poor sleep was associated with emotional exhaustion, impaired concentration and perceived patient safety risks. Participants reported using pharmacological and non-pharmacological strategies to manage fatigue and sleep difficulties. This study highlights that sleep disruption among nurses working in high-intensity settings is shaped by environmental, occupational, organisational, community and family-related factors. Poor sleep was perceived to be associated with emotional exhaustion, impaired concentration, patient safety concerns and reliance on adaptive and maladaptive coping strategies to manage fatigue and insomnia. These findings suggest that sleep disruption is a systemic issue requiring organisational and context-sensitive interventions to improve nurses' well-being and patient care outcomes. Improving nurses' well-being and patient safety requires interventions that address the organisational, environmental and social contributors to sleep disruption. Supportive practice environments, adequate staffing, fatigue management initiatives and psychosocial support may improve sleep quality, reduce emotional exhaustion and clinical errors and enhance nurse well-being and patient care outcomes.

papers.title: Strength in numbers: How intramolecular interactions help shape sodium channel biophysics.
Dual targeting of melatonergic and serotonergic neurotransmissions in Parkinson's disease: role of agomelatine.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder of the central nervous system (CNS), driven by the pathological aggregation and accumulation of α-synuclein (α-Syn) within dopaminergic neurons of the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc). Despite extensive research, the pathogenesis of PD remains incompletely understood and involves complex molecular signaling pathways. Melatonin and serotonin are dysregulated in PD and may contribute to cognitive impairment, sleep disturbances, and neuropsychiatric manifestations. Accordingly, restoration of melatonergic and serotonergic neurotransmission may support the management of depressive symptoms, cognitive impairment, and sleep disorders in patients with PD. Agomelatine, used in the management of major depressive disorder, can modulate both melatonergic and serotonergic neurotransmission. However, its molecular mechanisms and potential effects on the development and progression of PD have not been comprehensively evaluated. A literature search was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar from database inception to July 2026, using relevant keywords and MeSH terms related to PD, melatonergic and serotonergic neurotransmission, and agomelatine. Therefore, this narrative review discusses the role of melatonergic and serotonergic neurotransmission in PD and examines how targeting these pathways with agomelatine may contribute to PD management.

papers.title: Real-world performance of a ring-type cuffless blood pressure device compared with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring.
papers.abstract: Cuffless blood pressure (BP) monitoring devices are convenient alternatives to conventional ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM). We evaluated the real-world agreement between a ring-type cuffless BP device (continuous ambulatory ring-type blood pressure monitor, CART BP pro) and ABPM and identified the clinical and physiological factors associated with measurement discrepancies. This real-world observational study included 154 adults (mean age, 62.1 ± 14.2 years; 41.6% men) who underwent simultaneous 24-hour ABPM and CART BP pro after exclusion of predefined clinical conditions and insufficient recordings. CART BP pro measurements were calibrated at baseline to ABPM in the contralateral arm. BP values from the 2 devices were compared for 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime periods, as well as for the classification of nocturnal hypertension and dipping status. Predictors of close systolic agreement (|24-hour systolic blood pressure [SBP] difference| ≤ 5 mmHg) were identified using multivariable logistic regression. CART BP pro-derived period summaries were lower than ABPM for systolic BP (-7.1 mmHg for 24-hour SBP) and showed a modest positive bias for diastolic BP. Only 33.1% of measurements met the ≤ 5 mmHg accuracy criterion. Daytime SBP showed a similar bias (-7.8 mmHg), whereas nighttime SBP differences were smaller (-1.7 mmHg). By contrast, diastolic BP was consistently higher with the CART BP pro, particularly at night (+4.8 mmHg). Older age, male sex, lower body mass index, and higher heart rate independently predicted a closer systolic agreement. The agreement for nocturnal hypertension was moderate (κ = 0.516), with an overall concordance of 76.0%. However, dipping concordance was limited, with the CART BP pro showing blunted nocturnal dipping compared with ABPM (mean, 3.7% vs. 7.8%). This exploratory, real-world study found that CART BP pro-derived period summaries showed lower SBP values and smaller nocturnal BP declines than ABPM. Because period-level aggregates were compared rather than simultaneous point-to-point measurements, these findings should not be interpreted as a formal accuracy validation of the device. Further studies are needed to establish device-specific diagnostic thresholds and prospectively validate the clinical interpretation of CART BP pro-derived period summaries for hypertension diagnosis and circadian BP phenotyping.

papers.title: A Qualitative Exploration of Clinicians' Perspectives on Obstructive Sleep Apnea Facilitators and Barriers to Care.
papers.abstract: Literature has suggested that children experience wide variation in diagnosis and treatment of obstructive sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), however, multidisciplinary perspectives on barriers and facilitators to care are not well delineated among clinicians. This qualitative study adhered to the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Participants were recruited until thematic saturation was achieved across the overall dataset. Key informant interviews were conducted with physicians and advanced practice providers from primary care, otolaryngology, and sleep medicine across academic and community practices in both rural and urban settings. Interview transcripts were analyzed using a combined deductive-inductive thematic approach. Sixteen clinicians participated (62.5% female, 50% private vs academic, mean years in practice 12.6 [SD 7.1]), of whom were 56% primary care providers, 31% otolaryngologists, and 13% sleep medicine specialists. Multilevel barriers to SDB care delivery were organized using the socioecological model. Among primary care providers, management of SDB varied considerably with limited use of clinical practice guidelines. Decisions to make a referral were influenced by geographic access to specialists. For clinicians with a large Spanish-speaking population, they frequently described language barriers as important obstacles that negatively affected parental interactions. Limited access to polysomnography was the most significant barrier noted by clinicians in all disciplines and led to changes in provider recommendations and clinical pathways. This qualitative study provides multidisciplinary clinician perspectives on barriers and facilitators to pediatric sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) care across the socioecological framework. The findings identify multilevel factors that shape care pathways and highlight actionable opportunities to improve access, including enhanced caregiver education, standardized referral practices, expanded access to polysomnography, and greater support for clinicians through evidence-based guidance and multidisciplinary collaboration.

papers.title: Incidence and Determinants of Post-Coronavirus Disease Syndrome by Disease Severity: An Ambispective Cohort Study from a Tertiary Care Hospital in Puducherry.
papers.abstract: Post-coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) condition, or long COVID, persists beyond the acute phase, impacting quality of life. This study estimated the incidence and determinants of post-COVID syndrome (PCS) in Puducherry, India. This ambispective cohort study from May to December 2022 included 1162 adults with COVID-19. Participants were stratified by disease severity (moderate/severe and mild) based on clinical parameters during acute illness. We conducted follow-ups at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. PCS was defined as having ≥two of five common symptoms (fatigue, joint/muscle pain, breathing difficulty, loss of smell/taste, or sleep problems). Relative risks (RR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated using binomial regression with a Poisson link, adjusting for socio-demographic and clinical factors. Incidence of PCS was consistently higher in the moderate/severe group. At 1, 3, 6, and 12 months, incidence was 65.6%, 37.7%, 24.4%, and 34.4% for moderate/severe cases, and 24.3%, 11.0%, 7.1%, and 16.9% for mild cases, respectively. Moderate/severe cases had significantly higher RR of 2.70 at 1 month (95% CI: 2.31-3.15), 3.42 at 3 months (95% CI: 2.65-4.40), 3.46 at 6 months (95% CI: 2.49-4.80), and 2.04 at 12 months (95% CI: 1.65-2.52), all P < 0.001. Independent risk factors for PCS included rural residence, comorbidities, complications during hospitalization, and age over 30 years. Moderate/severe COVID-19 severity and specific socio-demographic and clinical factors were associated with an elevated risk of PCS. Early identification and targeted follow-up are recommended to mitigate long-term impacts.
papers.journal: Indian journal of community medicine : official publication of Indian Association of Preventive & Social Medicine

papers.title: [Differential diagnosis between Bipolar Disorder and behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia: the role of longitudinal neuropsychological assessment. A Case Report.].
papers.abstract: Bipolar Disorder (BD) and the behavioral variant of Frontotemporal Dementia (bvFTD) can present overlapping clinical features in their early stages, characterized by disinhibition, euphoria, and executive function deficits. Differential diagnosis is particularly challenging when behavioral symptoms are accompanied by evidence of cortical atrophy on neuroimaging. We describe the case of a 48-year-old woman diagnosed with Type I BD since age 25, referred for suspected bvFTD due to a progressive decline in memory functions and sleep disturbances. At the time of evaluation (T0), the patient had been on long-term treatment with aripiprazole, paroxetine, chlorpromazine, and clonazepam. A brain MRI was performed, and a second-level neuropsychological battery was administered to assess memory, attention, executive functions, language, and praxic functions. The entire protocol was repeated after two years (T1). At T0, analysis revealed marked deficits in executive functions, complex attention, and episodic memory; MRI showed moderate bilateral frontoparietal cortical atrophy. At follow-up (T1), despite the structural finding of atrophy, a complete normalization of the cognitive profile was observed, with performance returning to within normal limits for age and education. The longitudinal improvement confirms that the deficits detected at T0 were an expression of the clinical state of BD rather than a progressive neurodegenerative process. This case emphasizes the fundamental importance of longitudinal neuropsychological assessment and a multidisciplinary approach to avoid misdiagnosis and to optimize the pharmacological treatment of affective and psychotic symptoms.

papers.title: Relative Brain Perfusion Differences in a Patient With Persistent Cognitive Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Persistent cognitive symptoms in older adults may occur in the setting of multiple overlapping neurologic, vascular, sleep-related, psychiatric, and medical factors. We report the case of a 69-year-old man with several years of progressive short-term memory difficulty, cognitive slowing, word-finding difficulty, reduced decisiveness, and collateral concern regarding gait change. The clinical evaluation identified several potentially relevant contributors, including persistent dyslipidemia, inadequately treated obstructive sleep apnea, mild depressive symptoms, and a reported prior cerebrovascular finding. Portions of the outside diagnostic evaluation were unavailable for independent review. Brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT), obtained as an adjunctive component of the clinical evaluation, demonstrated a nonspecific mixed pattern of relative cortical and subcortical tracer-distribution differences. An individualized management plan was subsequently implemented, focusing on potentially modifiable contributors, sleep optimization, lifestyle measures, and depressive symptoms. At approximately three-month follow-up, the patient's spouse reported no significant memory improvement but no noticeable decline; subsequent follow-up raised renewed concern regarding progression. Because repeat standardized cognitive testing was not performed and multiple interventions were introduced over time, the longitudinal clinical course could not be objectively quantified or attributed to any individual intervention. This case describes a nonspecific pattern of relative brain perfusion differences in a patient with persistent cognitive symptoms. The relationship between these imaging findings and the patient's clinical symptoms remains uncertain, and this single observation does not establish a specific neurologic etiology or the diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment-selection utility of brain perfusion SPECT.
keywords: brain perfusion single-photon emission computed tomography (spect)

papers.title: Construction of a readmission prediction model and development of a decision support system for chronic heart failure patients based on patient-reported outcome measures.
papers.abstract: To construct a readmission risk prediction model for heart failure based on an Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) framework and develop a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) integrating Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROM), aiming to address the limitations of traditional models in processing multidimensional physiological-psychological-social data and their low clinical translation efficiency. A retrospective cohort study design was employed, enrolling 552 chronic heart failure patients (training-to-testing set ratio of 8:2). Multidimensional features were collected via electronic medical records and the Chinese version of the Heart Failure-Specific PROM Scale (CHF-PROM). Missing data were handled using Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE). An AutoML framework driven by an Improved Pied Kingfisher Optimizer (IPKO) algorithm, integrating algorithms including Logistic Regression, Support vector machine (SVM), XGBoost, and LightGBM, was developed. Model performance and interpretability were evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), Decision Curve Analysis (DCA), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). A visualized decision-making tool was implemented on the MATLAB platform. Testing set showed the AutoML model achieved significantly enhanced predictive efficacy [AUC = 0.8909, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.8392 to 0.9426]. SHAP analysis revealed key multidimensional factors influencing prognosis, among which milder depressive symptoms, higher levels of social support, and favorable appetite-sleep status were important protective factors reducing readmission risk, while female sex and advanced age were identified as risk predictors. Decision curve analysis further confirmed that applying this model yielded positive net clinical benefit across a wide risk threshold range of 1.2% to 78.6%. This study achieved efficient translation of PROM data into clinical decisions and innovatively demonstrated the independent predictive value of psychosocial factors for readmission. The developed CDSS system provides a feasible pathway for the proactive prevention and management of heart failure.

papers.title: Clinical Advantages and Pitfalls of Pulsed Field Ablation: How to Prevent ALH Syndrome.
papers.abstract: Catheter ablation for tachyarrhythmias was first introduced in the early 1980s using direct-current (DC) energy. Following the clinical introduction of radiofrequency (RF) ablation in the late 1980s, thermal ablation technologies became the foundation of catheter ablation because of their superior controllability, efficacy, and safety. In 2014, Wittkampf developed a DC-energy-delivery catheter system preventing electrical arcing, thereby initiating a modern "revival of DC-ablation" based on catheter ablation using electroporation. Subsequent development of high-voltage, short-duration pulse-train delivery led to the emergence of pulsed field ablation (PFA). Exposure of myocytes to high-voltage electric fields induces reversible electroporation through nanoscale pore formation within the lipid bilayer, whereas higher electric-field delivery produces irreversible electroporation, resulting in permanent membrane disruption, apoptosis, and durable lesion formation. PFA is regarded as a predominantly nonthermal and potentially tissue-selective ablation modality. Nevertheless, clinical trials of pulmonary vein isolation for atrial fibrillation have demonstrated that PFA is noninferior to conventional thermal ablation strategies, although clear superiority-other than shorter procedural times-has not yet been established. Importantly, recent studies suggest that electrode-tissue contact remains a critical determinant of durable lesion formation. Accumulating evidence indicates that PFA is associated with new complications not commonly observed with thermal ablation, including acute kidney injury, stroke, coronary vasospasm, myocardial ischemia, ventricular fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Although the mechanisms remain incompletely understood, hemolysis-related injury induced by high-voltage pulse delivery may represent an important contributing mechanism. Development of PFA systems capable of real-time prediction of irreversible lesion size may be essential for optimizing both procedural efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Smartphone-Measured Sleep Health Risk Factors Detect Suicidal Thoughts and Behaviors Among Adolescents.
papers.abstract: Suicide deaths and poor sleep health in adolescents have significantly increased. Smartphone sensors (eg, accelerometry) provide an unobtrusive and scalable way to monitor sleep health over extended time periods. We hypothesized that poor weekly sleep health (ie, shorter and variable time in bed; late and variable bedtime) assessed through smartphone sensors would associate with weekly suicidal thoughts and behaviors (STB). High-risk adolescents (N = 145, 13-18 years of age, 112 female) oversampled for STB (n = 114) installed the Effortless Assessment Research System application on their smartphones, allowing access to motion data over 6 months. Simultaneously, the app measured weekly suicidal ideation. Clinical interviews measured suicidal events (ie, attempts, specifc psychiatric hospitalizations, and emergency department events related to suicide risk) at 1-, 3-, and 6-month follow-up assessments. Mixed-effects logistic regression models tested whether the weekly average and variability of time in bed and bedtime related to next-week STB. A 1-SD in weekly time in bed, relative to one's typical weekly time in bed, related to a near 2-fold greater odds of a next-week suicidal event (odds ratio [OR] = 1.85, 95% CI = 1.01, 3.28, p = .045). This was driven by time in bed on weekdays (OR = 2.39, 95% CI = 1.19, 4.44, p = .013). Greater variability of bedtimes (ie, lower bedtime consistency) within a weekend, relative to one's own typical weekend bedtime variability, predicted next-week suicidal ideation (OR = 1.91, 95% CI = 1.28, 2.69, p = .001). Results reveal proximal associations between smartphone-derived sleep measures and STB, highlighting the possibility of developing just-in-time interventions, focusing on which sleep behaviors to modify and when to intervene to reduce suicide risk.

papers.title: Perioperative Airway Strategy for Madelung's Disease With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
Ketogenic diet therapy in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies: toward syndrome- and gene-informed precision therapy.
papers.abstract: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs) are severe, early-onset, frequently drug-resistant epilepsies in which recurrent seizures and epileptiform activity contribute to cognitive impairment beyond the underlying etiology. Ketogenic dietary therapies (KDTs) exert broad, multimodal antiseizure and neuroprotective effects and occupy a distinct position among nonpharmacologic treatments for DEEs. To synthesize the evidence for KDT across the principal electroclinical DEE syndromes, an expanding spectrum of gene-specific DEEs, and acute presentations such as febrile infection-related epilepsy syndrome (FIRES) and new-onset refractory status epilepticus (NORSE), with attention to outcome measures, mechanisms, adverse effects, and monitoring. A narrative review of the literature on the classic ketogenic diet (KD), modified Atkins diet, medium-chain triglyceride diet, and low-glycemic-index treatment in DEEs, drawing on randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses. KDT has the strongest and most methodologically rigorous evidence base in infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, including comparative-effectiveness data vs. hormonal therapy, followed by strong consensus supporting early use in epilepsy with myoclonic-atonic seizures. Meaningful benefit has also been reported in Dravet syndrome and, to a somewhat lesser extent, Lennox-Gastaut syndrome. Responses are more variable in early-infantile developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, epilepsy of infancy with migrating focal seizures, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation in sleep, and hemiconvulsion-hemiplegia-epilepsy syndrome, with tolerability and long-term adherence often declining over time. In FIRES/NORSE, KDT may serve as an acute anti-inflammatory treatment for super-refractory status epilepticus. Gene-specific responses vary substantially, with the most favorable outcomes observed in transporter-related disorders, followed by conditions involving other membrane-associated proteins, including ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors, whereas disorders affecting cellular structural integrity or homeostatic regulation appear less responsive. KDT has an increasingly well-supported, syndrome- and endpoint-specific role across DEEs. Future research should prioritize comparative-effectiveness trials, standardized outcome measures, predictors of response, better-tolerated formulations, and equitable access to dietary therapy.

papers.title: Validation of Pure and Total Movement Dispersion Variables as Measures of the Distribution of Daily Activity Using Accelerometers: A Secondary Analysis of a Prospective Cohort.
papers.abstract: Physical activity (PA) positively impacts health, but the optimal manner to achieve PA remains unclear. Pure and total movement dispersion are novel metrics that quantify the spread of movement across the day, with (total) or without (pure) intensity. The purpose of the study is to evaluate whether pure and total movement dispersion are positively associated with established PA metrics and inversely associated with sedentary behavior (SB) metrics. This study involves a secondary analysis of accelerometer data collected within the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS) from 2018 to 2020 in four U.S. cities (Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Pittsburgh) as part of a sleep substudy. Of the data received on 638 participants who wore an ActiGraph GT9X on their wrist for a period of seven days, 594 (93%) completed at least four valid wear days (≥10 hours/day) and were included in the analyses. Pure and total movement dispersion were calculated from raw accelerometer data utilizing an author-developed algorithm on a supercomputer and compared to average duration and bout length of moderate-vigorous intensity PA (MVPA) and SB, determined using the ActiLife platform with Montye cutpoints for adult wrist-worn activity, and active-to-sedentary (ASTP)/sedentary-to-active transition probability (SATP), previously calculated as part of the MACS sleep substudy. Due to the skewness of the data, Spearman's Rank correlations were computed to assess the relationships between pure and total movement dispersion and the established measures of PA and SB. Study activities were approved by Institutional Review Boards at each participating site, and all participants provided written informed consent for their data to be used in future studies. Participants (n = 594) had a mean age of 45 years (SD = 12) and 78 % were living with HIV. Pure movement dispersion demonstrated significant positive associations with PA measures (MVPA minutes: r s =.4056, p < .0001; MVPA bout: r s =.1708, p <.0001; SATP: r s =.5011, p <.0001) and negative with SB metrics (SB minutes: r s = -.0853, p =.0377; SB bout: r s =-.382, p <.0001; ASTP: r s = -.3837, p <.0001). Total movement dispersion exhibited stronger associations with PA measures (MVPA minutes: r s =.5719, p < .0001; MVPA bout: r s =.2844) and SB metrics (SB minutes: r s = -.2183, p <.0001; SB bout: r s = -.5039, p <.0001; ASTP: r s = -.4707, p <.0001). The strength of the relationships between the measures was weaker in those under 40 years old with pure movement dispersion and SB minutes (r s = -.1758, p =.2174) and MVPA bout (r s = .2451, p =.0829), and with total movement dispersion and MVPA bout (r s = .2565, p = .0692), no longer significantly associated. Both measures displayed expected associations with duration, intensity, and transition of PA and SB, supporting their convergent validity as a combined movement metric. These metrics can complement established measures to provide a richer context for PA behaviors and potentially explore the impact of varying dispersion levels on health outcomes. Future work will focus on establishing optimal ranges for both metrics that relate to positive health outcomes, such as changes in cardiovascular risk. Because the data are cross-sectional, causal inference cannot be established. Additionally, wrist-based accelerometer placement may bias intensity classification, and residual confounding from unmeasured lifestyle factors cannot be excluded.

papers.title: The implications of maternal sleep disruption on cardiovascular adaptations and cardiometabolic outcomes.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy involves profound physiological changes that, although necessary for gestation, might promote maladaptive systemic responses, an important consideration given rising maternal morbidity and mortality in the USA, and the role of cardiovascular disease as a leading cause of pregnancy-related death. This Personal View examines the link between disrupted peripartum sleep and adverse cardiometabolic outcomes. Sleep quality and duration often decline during pregnancy because of many factors, including hormonal changes, physical discomfort, and behavioural influences. Sleep pathologies, such as insomnia and sleep-disordered breathing, also become more common as pregnancy progresses. The transition from pregnancy to postpartum introduces a unique set of stressors, including newborn care and novel social demands and restrictions, which frequently compromise sleep quality. Persistent sleep disruption, during pregnancy or otherwise, should not be overlooked, as emerging evidence links poor sleep with increased inflammation, altered autonomic regulation, and impaired metabolic function. In the context of pregnancy, such processes are closely linked to the development of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, gestational diabetes, and increased cardiovascular risk across the lifespan. Although the number of studies assessing the role of sleep are increasing, important gaps remain in defining optimal perinatal sleep and identifying effective interventions to improve maternal sleep. Greater attention to sleep health within routine perinatal care, along with continued research in this area, is an important step towards improving maternal cardiovascular outcomes.
papers.journal: The Lancet. Obstetrics, gynaecology, & women's health

papers.title: From retina to brain: retinal dysfunction and dopaminergic neurodegeneration in Drosophila models of Parkinson's disease.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by the progressive loss of dopaminergic neurons within the substantia nigra pars compacta. Although PD is primarily defined as a motor disorder, prodromal non-motor symptoms - such as circadian clock desynchronization and sleep disturbances - can emerge years before clinical diagnosis. Increasing evidence suggests that these non-motor manifestations, particularly circadian disruption, may contribute to disease progression. However, it remains unclear whether circadian dysfunction actively drives neurodegeneration or arises as a consequence of ongoing neuronal loss. In this study, we employed genetic models of PD in Drosophila melanogaster to investigate these relationships. Specifically, we examined the effects of parkin (park) silencing and neuronal expression of human α-Synuclein on photoreceptor morphology and function. Furthermore, we assessed whether mitophagy impairment or synucleinopathy confined to the visual system can influence the onset and progression of PD-related phenotypes. Given that sleep fragmentation is a common feature in PD patients, we also analyzed sleep patterns in flies, focusing on sleep duration. In parallel, we evaluated dopaminergic neuron degeneration, with particular emphasis on the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster, which plays a critical role in the regulation of sleep and locomotor activity. Taken together, our findings highlight the importance of elucidating the interplay between retinal cells disruption and neurodegeneration in deeper parts of the brain in Parkinson's disease.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: The challenges of magnetic resonance imaging and the promise of portable neurotechnology for advancing scientific discovery about neurodevelopmental disorders.
Association of Lifestyle and Sociodemographic Factors with Menopause-specific Quality of Life: A Community-based Cross-Sectional Study from Northern India.
papers.abstract: Menopause-specific quality of life (MENQOL) in middle-aged women gives us an outline of ramifications of menopause in their life. This study was aimed at assessing the MENQOL among middle-aged women in urban Meerut and to determine the association of sociodemographic and lifestyle factors with MENQOL. A cross-sectional study among middle-aged women was conducted in the urban area of Meerut. The estimated sample size was 300. Study subjects were selected by a multistage sampling method. Data collection was done using a pre-tested and semi-structured questionnaire. Association was assessed using the Chi-square test and logistic regression analysis. Overall mean ± standard deviation score of MENQOL among study subjects was 3.1 ± 1.2. Women sleeping <5 hours in a day were 2.241 times more likely to have a poor quality of life (AOR: 2.241). In the psychosocial domain, lower middle class (AOR: 5.316) and lower class (AOR: 5.732) categories of socioeconomic classification revealed a robust association with poor psychosocial MENQOL in comparison with upper class women, with P values of 0.002 and 0.021, respectively. Tobacco users were significantly (P = 0.019) more likely (Adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 4.247) to encounter a poor sexual quality of life. Half of the study participants had a good MENQOL, with significant differences in MENQOL among the different domains. It was found that shorter sleep duration impacted overall MENQOL. Domain-wise analysis showed socioeconomic status in the psychosocial domain and marital status, occupation, and tobacco usage in the sexual domain as significant predictors.
papers.journal: Indian journal of community medicine : official publication of Indian Association of Preventive & Social Medicine

papers.title: Lamotrigine-associated severe cholestatic drug-induced liver injury requiring artificial liver support and percutaneous biliary drainage: a Case Report.
papers.abstract: Lamotrigine is widely used as an antiseizure medication, but it may rarely cause severe hypersensitivity reactions with systemic involvement. We report a 29-year-old male with epilepsy confirmed by brain MRI and EEG, who developed fever and generalized maculopapular rash during lamotrigine titration (2024-11-01), followed by progressive jaundice, severe pruritus, marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, cholestatic liver enzyme elevation, and coagulation dysfunction. Viral hepatitis and autoimmune liver diseases were excluded. Complete RegiSCAR scoring, RUCAM scale and WHO-UMC causality assessment were performed to confirm definite DRESS and lamotrigine-induced cholestatic DILI. Although lamotrigine was promptly discontinued (2024-11-07) and standard medical therapy was initiated, the patient developed refractory cholestatic drug-induced liver injury with dynamically evolving biliary tract abnormalities on serial imaging obtained at specific time points. He received repeated artificial liver support using a dual plasma molecular adsorption system combined with plasma exchange (detailed dates of each session are listed in and the clinical timeline). Because of persistent cholestasis and imaging evidence of impaired bile drainage, ultrasound-guided percutaneous transhepatic biliary drainage and subsequent hepatic duct drainage were performed (2024-11-26, outside West China Hospital; original MRCP and intraoperative PTCD images are unavailable due to hospital privacy regulations, and detailed textual descriptions of all biliary imaging and drainage procedures are supplemented), after which bilirubin levels, bile acids, aminotransferases, and coagulation parameters gradually improved. The clinical improvement was the combined effect of multiple sequential interventions including drug withdrawal, glucocorticoids, artificial liver support and PTCD, rather than being attributed solely to biliary drainage. This case suggests that lamotrigine-associated hypersensitivity-related liver injury may, in rare circumstances, progress to severe cholestatic DILI with evolving biliary tract involvement. Imaging manifestations raise suspicion of potential large-biliary tract inflammatory injury and early fibrotic changes with theoretical risk of secondary biliary cirrhosis; definitive diagnoses of large-duct obstruction, fibrotic biliary stenosis, or vanishing bile duct syndrome cannot be established without histopathological liver and biliary tract specimens. Repeated biliary imaging and multidisciplinary management should be considered when cholestasis persists or worsens despite drug withdrawal and conservative therapy. We also systematically discuss the central role of cytokine imbalance in DRESS pathogenesis and the clinical prospect of cytokine-targeted inhibitors for severe refractory cases, as well as long-term management strategies to improve long-term quality of life of such patients.

papers.title: Denture hygiene knowledge, cleaning practices, and denture stomatitis among primary care patients in Alkharj, Saudi Arabia: compliance predictors, barriers and educational preferences: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Denture wearers must maintain good denture hygiene, as oral health significantly impacts systemic health; yet denture hygiene practices remain poorly addressed within dental primary care facilities. Saudi Arabia's dental primary care system serves a demographically diverse population, including a large proportion of non-Saudi patients, creating a setting in which sociodemographic, linguistic, and economic factors intersect to shape the oral health behaviors of individuals who wear dentures. To assess denture hygiene knowledge, cleaning behaviors, and denture stomatitis among denture wearers attending a single primary care setting in Alkharj, Saudi Arabia, and to identify behavioral predictors and patient-reported barriers to denture hygiene compliance. A cross-sectional study of 120 patients attending a dental primary care clinic was conducted. A questionnaire assessed knowledge, barriers, and educational preferences about oral/denture hygiene care. A clinical examination assessed prosthetic history and classified denture stomatitis using the Newton system. Statistical analyses included independent t-tests, one-way ANOVA, Pearson correlation, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression (p = 0.05). Only 24.2% of patients demonstrated adequate knowledge of oral/denture hygiene. In comparison, high-income patients had significantly higher mean knowledge scores than low-income patients (p < .001); in the adjusted multivariable model, income level and nationality were each independently associated with knowledge adequacy. Young females (age <50 years) showed significantly higher oral/denture hygiene compliance (p < 0.001). 63.3% of patients reported wearing their denture during sleep due to forgetfulness, and 65.8% suffer from denture stomatitis. Written instructions were preferred by 51.7% of patients, and teaching hospitals were the main source of oral/denture care instructions. The most commonly mentioned barrier to receiving comprehensive oral/denture hygiene instruction was "dentists have no time to give instructions" (40.8%). Denture hygiene compliance is critically low among patients attending primary care settings in Alkharj, Saudi Arabia. Non-Saudi nationality, low income, greater tooth loss, and male sex are independent correlates of non-compliance. Forgetfulness regarding nighttime removal and social embarrassment about public denture cleaning represent prevalent behavioral barriers to non-compliance. The strong preference for written educational materials and the high prevalence of denture stomatitis collectively underscore the clinical and public health imperative for integrating brief, culturally adapted, written denture hygiene counseling into routine primary care in Saudi Arabia.

papers.title: I think, therefore I hit: EEG parameters predict performance in complex cognitive tasks.
papers.abstract: In recent years, operator state assessment has gained much attention in the aviation domain. The ability to assess or even predict performance from behavioral or physiological data offers the possibility to tailor training schedules and assistance systems to the human operators' needs. Yet, to date, there is still no valid or reliable method for such an assessment. In the present study, we present evidence that brain activity recorded via electroencephalography (EEG) can be used to predict complex cognitive task performance. 26 participants performed multiple rounds of a dual n-back task and the complex Space Fortress Game while their brain activity was recorded via EEG. Results from multiple linear regression analyses indicate that Space Fortress Game performance could be predicted reasonably well from EEG Power Spectral Density parameters from the same game, a previous game and from the dual n-back task. Our findings show that it is possible to use data from task training and even from dissimilar, less complex tasks to predict complex task performance (in offline analyses after data collection). They also underline the utility of using EEG measurements for operator state monitoring.

papers.title: Cross-sectional associations of maladaptive sleep-hygiene behaviors with athlete engagement among provincial- and municipal-level athletes in Sichuan, China.
papers.abstract: Maladaptive sleep-hygiene behaviors are potentially modifiable daily practices, yet their relationship with the psychological state that sustains sport involvement remains unclear. This study examined cross-sectional associations among maladaptive sleep-hygiene behaviors (MSHB), multidimensional fatigue, difficulties in emotion regulation, and athlete engagement, including three model-based indirect associations. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey was completed by 317 adult athletes recruited from provincial- and municipal-level teams in Sichuan Province, China. Participants represented table tennis, badminton, tennis, basketball, volleyball, and football. The Sleep Hygiene Index, the Chinese Multidimensional Fatigue Inventory, the DERS-16, and the Athlete Engagement Questionnaire were administered. A reflective partial least squares structural equation model was estimated with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Measurement quality, construct differentiation, common-method diagnostics, out-of-sample prediction, demographic adjustment, alternative cross-sectional specifications, and subgroup robustness were evaluated. More frequent MSHB were associated with greater fatigue [β = 0.491, 95% CI (0.408, 0.573)], greater difficulties in emotion regulation [β = 0.178, 95% CI (0.079, 0.274)], and lower athlete engagement [β = -0.264, 95% CI (-0.370, -0.161)]. Fatigue was associated with greater difficulties in emotion regulation [β = 0.588, 95% CI (0.500, 0.673)] and lower engagement [β = -0.325, 95% CI (-0.446, -0.205)]; difficulties in emotion regulation were also associated with lower engagement [β = -0.232, 95% CI (-0.351, -0.108)]. The total indirect association was [β = -0.268, 95% CI (-0.338, -0.204)], and the model explained 47.2% of engagement variance. Demographic adjustment yielded comparable estimates. Reverse-order and parallel specifications fitted the cross-sectional covariance structure equally well. Within the sampled setting, more frequent MSHB co-occurred with greater fatigue, more difficulties in emotion regulation, and lower athlete engagement. Fatigue accounted for the largest specific indirect association. The single-occasion self-report design leaves actual sleep disturbance, temporal sequence, and causal effects unresolved.

papers.title: Nutritional status, body composition and bone health in treatment-naïve transgender and gender-diverse adolescents.
papers.abstract: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone analogue (GnRHa)-induced gonadal suppression is an established component of gender-affirming care for transgender and gender-diverse (TGD) adolescents. Impaired bone health has been documented in treatment-naïve TGD adolescents prior to GnRHa intervention, yet its nutritional determinants remain poorly characterized. To characterize nutritional status, body composition, and bone mineral density (BMD) in treatment-naïve TGD adolescents prior to GnRHa initiation, and to identify predictors of lumbar spine BMD z-scores. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 147 treatment-naïve TGD adolescents (59 AMAB[TGD-Female] and 88 AFAB[TGD-Male]) attending a national pediatric gender clinic. Assessments included anthropometrics, body composition, 24-h dietary calcium intake (compared to the age-specific dietary reference intake [DRI]), micronutrient status, physical activity, sleep duration, and lumbar spine BMD z-scores by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Multiple linear regression identified predictors of BMD z-score, with sex assigned at birth included as a covariate. Descriptive analyses were conducted by sex assigned at birth. The median age was 15.5 years (IQR, 14.1-16.7), and 83.7% were fully pubertal. The median daily calcium intake was 400 mg/d (31% of the DRI), with 99.3% consuming below the DRI. Vitamin D deficiency/insufficiency was present in 91.5% of participants. Of the 102 participants with complete micronutrient data, 63.7% had ≥ 2 nutritional deficiencies. Body composition assessment revealed a below-average muscle-to-fat ratio in both groups (median z-score -0.74) and a higher fat mass percentage in AFAB compared to AMAB adolescents (28.6% vs. 17.4%; p < 0.001). The overall median BMD z-score was -0.70 (IQR, -1.30 to 0.10), with the AMAB adolescents having lower BMD z-scores than the AFAB adolescents (-1.00 vs. -0.40; p = 0.001), and 55.8% of the former having below-average/low BMD values compared with 33.0% of the latter (p = 0.015). The multivariable regression revealed that the BMI z-score (B = 0.403; p < 0.001) and sex assigned at birth (B = 0.372; p = 0.019) were the only independent predictors of the BMD z-score (R2 = 0.344, adjusted R2 = 0.318). Treatment-naïve TGD adolescents exhibit nutritional deficiencies, unfavorable body composition, and reduced BMD prior to GnRHa initiation, particularly those assigned male at birth. BMI z-scores and sex assigned at birth independently predicted BMD, highlighting the need for targeted pre-treatment nutritional and lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Toward Personalized Surgeons' Cognitive Workload: A Linear Mixed-Effects Model Analysis of EEG Features.
papers.abstract: Surgical Flow Disruptions in the operating room can increase cognitive workload and the risk of technical errors. While electroencephalography (EEG) provides an objective framework for monitoring mental effort, traditional statistical methods often rely on group-level analysis. This approach potentially ignores the significant degree of inter-subject variability among individuals. This study evaluated the effectiveness of various EEG features in monitoring the impact of SFDs using a Linear Mixed-Effects Model (LMEM) framework to distinguish between group trends and individual-specific responses. EEG data were recorded from nine surgical trainees during a simulated microvascular anastomosis, during which participants were subjected to six predefined SFDs, including auditory alerts and visual distractions. EEG features were analyzed using LMEM with random intercepts and slopes, and a subjectivity index was introduced to quantify the degree of individualization across 36 extracted EEG features. An initial analysis of variance on the fixed effects revealed that, generally, theta and beta power bands were significantly impacted by disruptions across the group. However, the subjectivity index identified several features, such as Gamma Asymmetry, that exhibited high individualization despite the absence of a significant group trend. Features characterized by both significant fixed effects and high subjectivity indices, such as Mean Power Beta, were identified as the most reliable metrics for tracking cognitive load. These results demonstrate that traditional group-averaging methods can mask critical individual physiological responses. By utilizing LMEM and the associated subjectivity index, this research establishes a statistical foundation for developing personalized intraoperative monitoring systems tailored to a surgeon's unique cognitive profile.

papers.title: Healthy lifestyle attenuates the clonal hematopoiesis-associated coronary artery disease risk.
papers.abstract: Lifestyle factors and clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) both contribute to the risk of developing coronary artery disease (CAD), but whether a healthy lifestyle could attenuate CHIP-related CAD risk is unknown. A total of 6113 participants from the Prediction for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Risk in China project were included. Lifestyle was categorized as unfavorable, intermediate, and favorable according to the number of healthy lifestyle factors (body mass index, smoking, sleep, physical activity, and diet). CHIP mutations were detected by targeted deep sequencing (mean depth, 916 ×). After a median follow-up of 12.1 years, 760 cases of CAD were recorded. A favorable lifestyle and CHIP were associated with 53% lower (HR (hazard ratio) = 0.47; 95% CI (confidence interval): 0.36-0.61) and 41% higher (HR = 1.41; 95% CI: 1.17-1.72) CAD risk, respectively. Of note, the elevated CAD risk attributed to CHIP was found in the intermediate (HR = 1.48; 95% CI: 1.03-2.11) and unfavorable (HR = 1.57; 95% CI: 1.22-2.01) lifestyle groups, but not in the favorable (HR = 0.71; 95% CI: 0.36-1.42) group. Unfavorable lifestyle and CHIP jointly contributed to a 2.78-fold increased risk of CAD (95% CI: 1.95-3.97) compared with non-CHIP carriers with a favorable lifestyle, indicating a significant additive interaction between CHIP and lifestyle (RERI (relative excess risk due to interaction) = 1.08; 95% CI: 0.40-1.77). Specifically, the protective effect of lifestyle depends on the size of cell fractions, with an intermediate lifestyle mitigating CAD risk in small clone carriers (VAF (variant allele fraction): 0.5%-2%), and a favorable lifestyle being necessary for common clone carriers (VAF ≥ 2%). In summary, CHIP carriers exhibited a higher risk of CAD, while a favorable lifestyle could attenuate the excess risk related to CHIP. Efforts should be made to promote intensive behavioral interventions among CHIP carriers.

papers.title: Effects of school-based active breaks on motor competence, physical fitness, academic outcomes, and health behaviors in Chilean preschoolers: protocol for a three-arm, non-randomized cluster-controlled mixed-methods trial.
papers.abstract: Although school-based physical activity (PA) is associated with improvements in multiple health and learning indicators, significant gaps persist regarding its systematic implementation at the preschool level. This protocol presents the rationale and methodological design of a curriculum-integrated active break program aimed at evaluating its impact in 5- to 6-year-old preschoolers. A three-arm, non-randomized cluster-controlled trial employing a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design (QUAN → qual) will be conducted in 12 urban public schools in the province of Biobío, Chile, involving 200 kindergarten preschoolers. Primary outcomes-motor competence and health-related physical fitness-and secondary outcomes-learning outcomes and healthy habits (sleep, eating behavior, nutritional status)-will be assessed at baseline and post-intervention. Over 16 weeks, children in the Total Experimental Group (TEG; 4 schools, n = 67) will complete 10 active breaks per week; the Partial Experimental Group (PEG; 3 schools, n = 66) will complete 3-5 active breaks per week; and the Control Group (CG; 5 schools, n = 67) will continue regular daily routines. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first controlled trial to simultaneously examine the efficacy of a curriculum-integrated active break program on motor competence, physical fitness, learning outcomes, and healthy habits in preschool-aged children. The inclusive design, digital platform support, and mixed-methods approach position this trial as a novel contribution to the evidence base for early childhood PA interventions and educational public policy. Open Science Framework (OSF). Unique identifier: cu6za. Public URL: https://osf.io/cu6za/overview.

papers.title: Links between psychological distress, late chronotype, and impaired sleep quality in survivors of sexual assault.
papers.abstract: Sexual assault is a pervasive issue with profound psychological and physical impacts, including significant sleep disturbances. Although psychological distress is a well-established mediator in the relationship between sexual assault and poor sleep quality, the role of the circadian system remains underexplored. The circadian system manifests a continuum of sleep-wake cycles, with late chronotype being a particularly disruptive pattern linked to impaired psychological functioning. Severe psychological stress can disrupt our circadian system leading to emergence of late chronotype preference. This study investigates whether psychological distress and late chronotype mediate the relationship experiences of sexual assault and sleep quality using a cross-sectional design. Canadian participants (n = 90 with sexual assault history; n = 97 controls; 19-50 years) were recruited via crowdsourcing. Structural equation modelling confirmed that sexual assault was significantly related to greater levels of psychological distress, psychological distress significantly predicted late chronotype, but only psychological distress (and not late chronotype) mediated the relationship between sexual assault and poor sleep quality. Although the contribution of late chronotype to sleep quality was not clarified, this study made clear that this maladaptive chronotype is prevalent among survivors and associated with distress. Implications are discussed in terms of the long-term impacts of sexual assault, including sleep-focused interventions to improve outcomes for survivors, and the value of studying sleep quality among those suffering from traumatic events.

papers.title: Identification of prognostic factors associated with contemporary lifestyles in community-dwelling young stroke survivors.
papers.abstract: Over the past few decades, the global incidence of stroke among young adults (aged 18-50 years) has risen significantly. Given their prolonged post-stroke life expectancy, this trend has resulted in a substantial burden of long-term disability. Beyond traditional vascular prognostic factors, unhealthy modern lifestyles are increasingly contributing to this trend. This study enrolled community-dwelling adults from three communities in Guangzhou, who were stratified into a young adult group (aged 18-49 years) and an older adult group (aged ≥50 years). Baseline questionnaires were administered to collect demographic characteristics, educational attainment, occupation, medical and family histories, lifestyle factors, and the Essen Stroke Risk Score (ESRS). During a one-year telephone follow-up, we assessed the recurrence of stroke, modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores, and changes in the ESRS from baseline. Young adults exhibited higher educational attainment and a distinct occupational distribution. The older adult cohort demonstrated a higher prevalence of preexisting medical conditions, as well as a more frequent family history of coronary heart disease and cancer. Young participants reported engaging in less physical exercise, domestic chores, and social interaction; however, they reported better sleep quality and a higher rate of cohabitation. In the unadjusted analysis, the young adult group exhibited a lower proportion of favorable functional outcomes (mRS 0-1: 60% vs. 65%), with an unadjusted odds ratio (OR) of 0.789 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.670-0.930]. However, this disparity was attenuated and became non-significant following adjustment, the OR was 0.904 (95% CI: 0.730-1.120, p = 0.355). Ischemic stroke recurrence rates were comparable between the two groups (4% vs. 6%), whereas the older group exhibited a more pronounced change in ESRS scores. The initially observed disparity in functional outcomes between young and older stroke patients appears to be heavily influenced by distinct, modifiable lifestyle factors. Early identification of and timely intervention against these prognostic factors are paramount for reducing the recurrence of stroke among young adults and minimizing its long-term sequelae.

papers.title: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation, tolerability, and the Alpha/Theta EEG ratio: a controlled pilot study relevant to emotion regulation.
papers.abstract: Anxiety and depression are both characterised by difficulties in emotion regulation, associated with altered cortical oscillatory activity. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) may modulate these dynamics, but few studies have examined stimulation intensity alongside both tolerability and EEG outcomes. In this controlled pilot, ten healthy female adults (21.1 ± 1.8 years) were randomized to taVNS (n = 5) or a waitlist control (n = 5). The taVNS group completed eight 30-minute left tragus sessions over four weeks (20 Hz, 200 μs, 14-25 mA, individually titrated), with Alpha/Theta and Theta/Beta ratios derived from resting-state EEG at Cz. We applied False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction across the exploratory comparisons. Protocol completion was 100% across 40 sessions. Of 39 stimulation-related observations, 29 were tolerability or adverse-event symptoms, predominantly CTCAE Grade 1 (86.2%); 10 were self-reported sensations of pulse change, recorded separately. None was serious. Within-group change in the taVNS group was not significant (exact p = .063 for both ratios). Stimulation intensity did not show a positive dose-response. Between-group comparisons of change scores favoured taVNS for both ratios (both U = 25, exact p = .008; Hodges-Lehmann median difference 0.56, 95% CI [0.12, 0.90] for Alpha/Theta) and remained significant after FDR correction. The protocol was completed by all five stimulated participants without serious adverse events under individual titration to tolerability (14-25 mA). We found preliminary effects on an EEG index relevant to emotion regulation, providing a quantitative basis for powering sham-controlled trials in clinical emotional dysregulation.

papers.title: Clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of Tuina for primary dysmenorrhea with cold congestion and blood stasis pattern: a protocol for a randomized controlled fMRI trial.
papers.abstract: Primary dysmenorrhea (PD) is one of the most common gynecological disorders in women of reproductive age and significantly impairs quality of life. Epidemiological data indicate that the cold congestion and blood stasis pattern accounts for a large proportion of PD cases. Tuina, a traditional Chinese external therapy, has unique advantages in pain management; however, its clinical efficacy and central mechanisms for PD remain unclear. This study aims to conduct an assessor-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial, integrating functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), to evaluate the clinical efficacy, safety, and central brain network modulation of Tuina therapy for primary dysmenorrhea with the cold congestion and blood stasis pattern. This study employed a randomized controlled trial design. A total of 54 patients who met the diagnostic criteria were recruited and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the treatment or control group. An additional 15 healthy women were included as the healthy group. Participants in the treatment group received standardized manipulation over two consecutive menstrual cycles. For each cycle, treatment began 7 days before menstruation and was administered once daily for 7 consecutive days. Participants in the control group received conventional oral ibuprofen, taken as needed for pain relief. The primary outcome was the change in the Visual Analog Scale score. Secondary outcomes included the COX Menstrual Symptom Scale, Traditional Chinese Medicine pattern score, sleep index, and psychological assessments. All outcomes were evaluated at three time points: baseline, after the first treatment cycle, and after the second treatment cycle. All participants underwent two fMRI sessions-both resting-state and task-state fMRI scans-during days 1-3 of their menstrual cycle: once before enrollment and once after the treatment period. All statistical analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. This study aims to provide high-level clinical evidence on pain relief, symptom improvement, and brain functional network regulation for the treatment of cold congestion stasis type dysmenorrhea with Tuina therapy, using a randomized controlled trial design combined with functional magnetic resonance imaging. https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn, International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry ITMCTR2026001387.
keywords: cold congestion and blood stasis pattern

papers.title: Neurosyphilis presenting as status epilepticus and hemiplegia diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing: A case report.
papers.abstract: The current study aimed to present a diagnostically challenging case of neurosyphilis manifesting with atypical neurological symptoms, emphasizing the importance of clinical vigilance and advanced diagnostics in avoiding misdiagnosis and inappropriate intervention. In the present study, a case of neurosyphilis, initially misdiagnosed and treated as acute cerebral infarction, is reported. Diagnostic analyses included serial brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), continuous electroencephalography (EEG) monitoring and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for pathogen identification. The results revealed that the patient presented with status epilepticus and hemiplegia. Follow-up MRI after transfer revealed extensive patchy cortical and subcortical white matter abnormalities in the right cerebral hemisphere. Notably, a thalamic signal abnormality observed on pre-thrombolysis diffusion-weighted imaging had notably diminished. EEG demonstrated periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs). CSF mNGS definitively identified 883 specific sequences of Treponema pallidum. Despite targeted anti-syphilitic and antiepileptic therapy, the patient's consciousness failed to improve, with persistent PLEDs on EEG. The patient was later discharged against medical advice due to pulmonary infection and hypotension and was subsequently confirmed deceased. In conclusion, the current case illustrates the markedly diverse and misleading presentations of neurosyphilis, which can mimic other acute neurological conditions. It underscores the need for maintaining a high index of suspicion and utilizing comprehensive diagnostic tools, including mNGS, to ensure accurate diagnosis and prevent the consequences of missed diagnosis or incorrect treatment.

papers.title: Neural signatures of auditory distraction and cognitive demand during working memory performance.
papers.abstract: Cognitive performance in real-world environments often requires maintaining working memory under simultaneous cognitive demand and environmental distraction. Although both factors have independently been associated with alterations in attention and executive control, their combined neural effects remain insufficiently understood. The present study investigated the influence of auditory distraction, time pressure, and their combination on working memory performance using a multidimensional electroencephalography (EEG) framework. Thirty healthy participants completed a working memory task under baseline, distraction, time-pressure, and combined conditions while EEG was recorded from 32 channels. Neural activity was characterized using oscillatory bandpower, topographical statistical mapping, hemispheric asymmetry, and weighted Phase Lag Index functional connectivity. Behavioral performance was complemented by subjective workload and stress assessments. Distraction was primarily characterized by widespread alpha-band suppression, significant frontal and parietal delta-band increases, and decreased frontal alpha asymmetry, whereas time pressure elicited frontal and parietal theta-band power increases. Rather than representing an additive superposition of both manipulations, the combined condition exhibited a distinct spatial pattern of oscillatory changes. Hemispheric asymmetry analyses revealed condition-dependent lateralization patterns that complemented conventional bandpower analyses. While alpha asymmetry primarily differentiated distraction, beta asymmetry emerged as the most consistent hemispheric marker across the experimental conditions showing regional beta-bandpower changes, highlighting the additional value of lateralized EEG measures for characterizing cognitive demands. Functional connectivity analyses did not reveal significant condition-dependent effects. These findings demonstrate distinct oscillatory signatures of distraction, time pressure, and their combination, highlighting the value of a multidimensional EEG framework for investigating concurrent cognitive demands.

papers.title: Effects of warm water footbath on sleep quality and fatigue in patients with heart failure: a randomized controlled study.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality and fatigue are common and clinically important problems in patients with heart failure (HF). Warm water footbaths are a form of local heat therapy that can induce comfort, relieve fatigue, and improve insomnia through heat conduction. This study aimed to explore the effects of a warm-water footbath (WWFB) on sleep quality and fatigue in patients with HF. A total of 86 patients with HF were randomized to the WWFB group (n = 43) or the control group (n = 43), and 74 completed follow-up. The WWFB group received a 42 °C warm-water footbath for 20 min each night for four weeks in addition to actigraphy monitoring, whereas the control group underwent actigraphy monitoring alone. Objective sleep parameters were recorded during the 4-week intervention, and subjective sleep quality and fatigue were assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 8. Compared with the control group, the WWFB group showed greater improvement in subjective sleep quality and fatigue over time. For objective sleep outcomes, sleep efficiency improved on several study days, and sleep latency was shorter on day 2, whereas total sleep time did not differ significantly between groups. WWFB is a non-invasive and simple intervention that was associated with improved subjective sleep quality and reduced fatigue in this study. These findings support WWFB as a potential adjunct to home or clinical care for patients with HF. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06287996, ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT06287996.

papers.title: Health behaviors of blood donors in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional comparative study with non-donors.
papers.abstract: Blood donation is essential for maintaining a safe and sustainable blood supply. Evidence suggests that blood donors may exhibit healthier lifestyle behaviors than non-donors (the healthy donor effect), but data from Saudi Arabia remain limited. This study compared lifestyle behaviors and health perceptions between blood donors and non-donors in Saudi Arabia. This cross-sectional study included 397 Saudi adults (265 blood donors and 132 non-donors) recruited between April and October 2024. Participants completed a structured questionnaire adapted from a previously published questionnaire assessing sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle behaviors, and donation-related beliefs. Associations between donor status and selected lifestyle outcomes were examined using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, BMI, education, occupation, and smoking where appropriate. Compared with non-donors, donors were more likely to report regular or daily physical activity (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.64, 95% CI 1.26-5.53), good or excellent meal quality (aOR 2.39, 95% CI 1.20-4.74), and good or excellent sleep quality (aOR 2.29, 95% CI 1.19-4.38). However, donors also had higher odds of regular smoking (aOR 2.81, 95% CI 1.16-6.79) and current smoking (aOR 3.62, 95% CI 1.69-7.75). Most donors (84.9%) believed that blood donation benefited their general health and activity. Blood donors reported more favorable behaviors related to physical activity, nutrition, and sleep than non-donors after adjustment for measured confounders. However, the higher prevalence of smoking among donors indicates that healthier behaviors do not extend uniformly across all lifestyle domains, and residual confounding related to baseline demographic differences cannot be excluded. Blood donation services may therefore provide valuable opportunities to integrate targeted health promotion and smoking cessation initiatives.

papers.title: Associations between pre-to-post TMS-evoked potential changes and motor sequence learning across retention intervals.
papers.abstract: Motor sequence learning involves practice-related changes in behavior and neural activity, yet the neurophysiological markers associated with later retention remain unclear. TMS-evoked potentials (TEPs) provide a measure of cortical responses to stimulation and may help characterize physiological-behavioral relationships across different learning timescales. Whether these associations differ across retention intervals remains unclear. We examined whether baseline TMS-EEG measures or task-related changes in right primary motor cortex (M1) TEPs are associated with initial acquisition and subsequent performance change across short and long-term retention intervals during a non-dominant hand motor sequence task. Seventeen healthy right-handed adults performed a five-element finger-tapping sequence with the left hand across three sessions: Day 1 (acquisition), Day 2 (short-term retention), and Day 7 (long-term retention). Single-pulse TMS-EEG was acquired before and after task performance over right M1 at each session. Four TEP components (N45, N100, P180, and N280) were analyzed. Day 1 training was associated with increases in PR and ACC, together with improved accuracy-adjusted efficiency, and slope dynamics remained broadly stable across later test sessions. Acute pre-to-post right-M1 TEP changes were not associated with rapid within-session acquisition. Pre-to-post P180 TEP change showed a nominal association with subsequent efficiency change, with a stronger nominal pattern over the 24-h interval than over the 5-day interval. However, neither the P180 dTEP effect nor the Interval × dTEP interaction survived FDR correction, and both were sensitive to participant-level influence and bootstrap resampling. These findings suggest that right-M1 TEP measures showed different relationships with rapid within-session acquisition and between-session performance change. Late P180 changes may be related to performance change across different retention intervals, but whether they reflect time-dependent consolidation processes remains to be established.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of alpha-band cortico-cortical coherence during motor preparation for successful and unsuccessful football penalty kicks.
papers.abstract: Successful motor performance may depend on the efficient coordination of cognitive and motor processes during movement preparation. Although previous electroencephalographic studies have linked alpha-band (8-13 Hz) coherence with performance in upper-limb precision tasks, little is known about cortico-cortical communication preceding successful lower-limb actions. Sixteen skilled football players performed penalty kicks under an individualized task-difficulty condition. EEG coherence was calculated for eight electrode pairs connecting the left and right temporal regions with frontal, central, parietal, and occipital midline sites. Coherence was examined during an early preparation period from -2,000 to -1,000 ms and a late preparation period from -1,000 to 0 ms before kick initiation. Successful kicks showed significantly lower Fz-T7 coherence than unsuccessful kicks across both preparation periods. Successful kicks also exhibited lower Cz-T8 coherence during the late preparation period. Lower Fz-T7 coherence may reflect reduced interaction between verbal-analytical processing and motor planning, whereas lower Cz-T8 coherence may indicate reduced coupling between visuospatial processing and motor-control processes immediately before kick initiation. These findings extend previous evidence from upper-limb precision tasks to football penalty kicking and support the psychomotor efficiency hypothesis. Successful kicking appears to be characterized by selective and time-dependent reductions in functional coupling rather than a general decrease in cortical connectivity.

papers.title: Integrating resting-state functional connectivity, mismatch negativity, and auditory steady-state responses reveals convergent neurophysiological biomarkers of schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia is a heterogeneous neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by abnormalities in large-scale brain connectivity, auditory prediction-error processing, and cortical gamma-band synchronization.
